label: pjm 34 coal rank
definition: pjm_33 lineage (forecast-grade reference-price interchange seam, MISO reanchor) + a CORRECTNESS fix to coal-rank labeling: three retiring PJM coal plants — W H Sammis (OH), Homer City (PA), AES Warrior Run (MD), all bituminous — were stuck in the model's generic unranked COAL bucket because coal_supply_class consulted only the curated + EIA-923 fuel-receipt maps, and a mid-backcast retiree has no recent burned-fuel receipts to derive a rank from. The EIA-923 benchmark already resolves them to COAL_BIT via fuel code, so the model showed a spurious generic 'Coal' row the actual never has AND priced them at generic full cost instead of PJM's bituminous passthrough. FIX (data.fleet.coal_supply_class): a tertiary EIA-860 energy_source fallback scoped to the retired-within-window vintage (the exact structural gap; operable coal untouched), mirroring the benchmark's fuel-code fallback. PJM coal now fully resolves (32 bituminous, 0 unranked); 212 fleet/coal tests pass. KEY FINDING — the dashboard's '+7%' 2023 coal-over was a LABELING ARTIFACT: the coal-tot gate sums only BIT+PRB+WC, so it compared model-coal-MINUS-the-3-retirees (~13 TWh hidden in the excluded generic bucket) against actual-coal-that-INCLUDES-them. Apples-to-apples the 2023 coal-over is +18.7% (+21 TWh), not +7%; total model coal barely moved (136.7->134.8 TWh, repricing ~dispatch-neutral) — only the attribution became honest. SCORECARD vs actual (coal-tot %; LMP %): 2023 coal-tot +18.7% (was +6.9%), COAL_BIT +20.0%, gas +2.2%, LMP +2.4%, net-export +29.6% | 2024 coal-tot +3.9% (was +1.0%, still PASS, 0 fails), LMP -6.3% | 2025 coal-tot +7.5% (UNCHANGED from pjm_33 — no retirees operating, so this is the GENUINE coal-over, not labeling), LMP -13.7%. in-tol fails 5 (same count as pjm_33; 2023 COAL_BIT/coal-tot, 2025 COAL_BIT/COAL_PRB/coal-tot). ROOT CAUSE now visible: ~half the 2023 coal-over is the 3 retirees over-dispatching (Homer City model 9.1 vs 1.0 TWh actual) — part a COD-ramp partial-retirement bug (load_cod_map collapses heterogeneous unit-retirement dates to the latest, so Homer City runs 2 units that retired Jul/Aug through year-end; small-scope 4-plant cross-ISO fix deferred), part the dominant economic over-dispatch of cheap uneconomic retirees the energy-only LP runs as baseload (needs CAMPD unit-level availability, not a fit). LMP/interchange unchanged vs pjm_33; this run makes the coal scorecard HONEST (faithfulness over MAE) and supersedes pjm_33's misleading coal-over.
